To secure
 an AI agent economy against Sybil attacks, networks can employ cryptographic stake-weighted verification acting like a digital jetty against flooding identities. Each agent must lock collateral onto a consensus thread to validate transactions. If an identity behaves maliciously, this stake is slashed. The attacker bears a linear financial cost proportional to the number of false nodes spawned, illuminating dishonest behavior like a beacon from a lantern and making mass-identity fabrication economically prohibitive.
